steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Economic growth is an increase in the value of goods and services produced in an economy over time, usually measured by GDP (Gross Domestic Product).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Real GDP adjusts for inflation (uses constant prices), giving a true picture of whether output actually increased. GDP per capita = GDP / population, indicating average living standards.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Causes of growth: increase in quantity/quality of factors of production, technological progress, increased investment, improved education and training, and population growth.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Benefits of growth: higher incomes, improved living standards, lower unemployment, increased tax revenue (for public services), and greater consumer choice.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always specify REAL GDP (adjusted for inflation) when discussing whether the economy has actually grown. GDP per capita is a better measure of living standards than total GDP — India has higher GDP than Switzerland but much lower GDP per capita. When evaluating growth, consider BOTH economic AND non-economic factors (environment, wellbeing).
